composition.story: How does k-means clustering work? Start with five points and two seeded centers. Assign each point to its nearest center, then replace centers with cluster means. Watch Point R switch after the centers move. Repeat until assignments stop changing. Use Previous and Next to compare the states.

aha.observation: Point R switches after the centers move; repeating assignment and mean updates ends with unchanged assignments.

parts.presentation: Place below the story and instructions, above the experiment. Use the canonical algorithm/collection composition. Highlight the active state; progress belongs here. State indices represent algorithm states, never elapsed time. Reference capture shows Stable.

Show fixed array cells P, Q, R, S, T, with Center A and Center B below. Each region displays its phases entry at the active step's index. Coordinates remain fixed; membership words change. Cell spacing does not encode distance. Use membership text and highlighting, never color alone. Fixed inputs are the displayed coordinates, k=2, and the centers shown in Seed. Assume one-dimensional Euclidean distance. Ties choose A; none occur here. No cluster becomes empty.
Anchor to the named active part without covering cells. Reserve wrapping space for every state. Identify the mechanism here; numerical measurements belong in the readouts.

Place measurements below the picture in two columns, followed by the bound status line. Positions and distances use arbitrary x-units and a common origin. Distances are absolute coordinate differences; centers are arithmetic means of assigned coordinates. Update arrows compare previous and current center positions; distances always use current centers. All displayed measurements are exact integers for these inputs. Balanced depth has zero parameter controls, excluding navigation and reset.

controls.label: Step
controls.presentation: Use Previous and Next, retaining their names when disabled at boundaries. Default is Seed; bounds are the listed states; increment is one state. Every state persists until learner action, including Stable. Provide visible focus and keyboard activation. Left Arrow selects Previous; Right Arrow selects Next.

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Restore Seed and all fixed defaults. Provide the accessible name Reset, visible focus, and keyboard activation.

states.label: Seed
states.sentence: Begin with seeded centers and unassigned points.
states.why: These fixed starting centers determine the first assignment; different seeds can produce different outcomes.

states.label: Assign
states.sentence: Assign each point to its nearest center; Point R joins Cluster B.
states.why: Keep centers fixed during assignment. P and Q choose A; R, S, and T choose B.

states.label: Update means
states.sentence: Replace each center with the mean of its assigned points.
states.why: Point R is now closer to A, but its membership remains B until the next assignment step.

states.label: Reassign
states.sentence: Point R switches to Cluster A because the updated Center A is nearer.
states.why: The other memberships stay unchanged. Moving the centers changed the nearest-center comparison for Point R.

states.label: Update means
states.sentence: Recompute both means using the changed memberships.
states.why: P, Q, and R determine Center A; S and T determine Center B. Membership stays fixed during this update.

states.label: Stable
states.sentence: Another nearest-center assignment changes nothing, so this run stops.
states.why: Every point remains nearest its assigned center, and both centers equal their assigned points' means.
